on_the_four_survivors: Each survived attacks that turned on the attacker. DBND-503: the refuter went looking for a reading of narrow that would rescue the phrase and found the specification defining it against the claim target. DBND-603: the refuter invented a sixth attack the brief had not suggested, killed it itself, and corrected two cosmetic errors while saying neither was load-bearing. DBND-701: the refuter found evidence the claimant had NOT used and which cuts the same way — row :143 asserts byte-equality against a golden vector under a sentence promising a signature verifies. DBND-709: the refuter established the specification enumerates exactly six confinement surfaces, verbatim, and that the outline exercises one; its steelman failed because cold_verify first store contact is list, whose confinement lives in different code from get.

round_1_remaining.decisive_fact: The claim was arithmetic — three Then steps contribute one net assertion — and the arithmetic is wrong. The helper compares gamma_delta against the vector field case[journalized] (cucumber.rs:3529, :3538); the Then compares it against a HARDCODED predicate on the operation name, matches!(operation, create|edit|delete) (cucumber.rs:11536). Two different sources, verified by the orchestrator. Nothing anywhere cross-checks the vector against the semantics, so the Then is the only thing in the suite that ties the sentence every mutation is journalized to anything real. Deleting it would turn a joint vector-and-production regression from red to green — the opposite of changes nothing.

The sibling row at features/d-bundle.feature:160, | FsStore | display path | folder/link-out/section |, installs its symlink at the INTERMEDIATE component and drives a store key that validate_store_key accepts, so checked_join per-segment symlink check is the sole defence that makes that row pass. The intermediate-symlink case IS tested by this outline. Verified by the orchestrator: both rows exist, :160 and :163. At most one row is mislabelled, and it still passes for a correct reason — the closed object grammar refusing the key is itself the confinement.

The claim states the ordering correctly and draws the opposite conclusion. The fixture RENAMES real bundle files inside root and replaces them with symlinks — e/circle/.index-original at cucumber.rs:3256, .manifest-original at :3268 — and core_path_raw_snapshot walks root recursively and is symlink-aware. So if the baseline were taken BEFORE the fixture as the claim demands, before == after would be false for every FsStore row even against perfectly correct code, and the assertion would fail unconditionally on 6 of 10 examples. The current ordering is the only one under which it can ever pass, and the only one that measures the operation effect rather than the test own attack input.
